answer: Each agent receives nontransferable work credits only after completing tasks that independent peers verify, and its credit history is tied to a costly stake that can be slashed for collusion. A pulse of randomly assigned reviews limits who can validate whose work; a ridge of trust forms only through repeated agreement across unrelated agents, while a lantern audit samples outcomes and exposes coordinated fakes. An attacker must fund many identities, produce useful work, and risk losing stake, so creating sybils does not cheaply create influence.
